name: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
label: Matador
lede: A Pussy Galore veteran, a guitarist from Appleton, Wisconsin and a drummer from Queens turned the blues into a New York noise machine with two guitars, drums and a theremin, and talked Beck, the Beastie Boys, R.L. Burnside and Weird Al into coming along.

eras.title: No bass player required
eras.text: Jon Spencer's five years in Pussy Galore included a cassette of the Rolling Stones' entire Exile on Main St., reportedly made on a dare. When the band ended in 1990 he met two players through The Honeymoon Killers, and the three started jamming with two guitars, drums and no bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pussy Galore · Wikipedia: Jon Spencer
years.h: Pussy Galore ends, and Historia de la Musica Rock is the last word
years.p: Jon Spencer's first band is done in 1990. He starts [[Boss Hog|57648c1f-335d-4216-ba82-508b23b3bcf4]] with Cristina Martinez, his wife since 1989, and keeps looking for his next thing.
years.xp: Pussy Galore started in 1985 with Spencer and Julia Cafritz, fellow Brown University students, and moved to New York in May 1986. Along the way it covered Exile on Main St. front to back on a limited cassette, reportedly on a dare from [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]]. Guitarist Neil Hagerty left for [[Royal Trux|87e27246-8c40-407f-bfb3-5dc416557eeb]].

years.big: "We just kind of stumbled into each other."
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Spencer, Bauer and Simins find each other through the Honeymoon Killers
years.p: Jon Spencer on how he met guitarist [[Judah Bauer|19c21a31-c2f6-446d-b989-f714715a836c]], from Appleton, Wisconsin, and drummer [[Russell Simins|f20a46bf-6f35-4bce-9fbb-b19de6fc3c0b]], from Queens, in a 1993 Fiz interview.
years.xp:
Simins was the drummer the Honeymoon Killers had found, Spencer told Fiz, and Bauer was the friend living with him. Spencer was coming around to play with the Killers; the three just started playing together.

By their first recording session, in July 1991, they'd been a band about six months.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Kramer records the trio in three hours, and skips the mixing board
years.p: At Noise New York in July 1991, the Blues Explosion cut fourteen songs for producer [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]], with almost no overdubs.
years.xp:
Kramer said they were "only doing second takes here and there, we didn't even go to the mixing board."

A second session followed in late 1991 with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] at Waterfront in Hoboken, New Jersey. The Kramer tapes got out first as a bootleg, A Reverse Willie Horton, in an edition of 500 or 1,000, with a negative image of Clarence Thomas's swearing-in on the cover.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Caroline and Hut release the first album, stitched from two sessions
years.p: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion pulls from the Kramer and Albini tapes. Germany's Crypt puts out a different cut under the name Crypt Style.

eras.title: Matador turns up the width
eras.text: Matador signed the band for America. In two years they went from studios in Memphis and New York to British television and an Australian tour with Beck, and Orange landed at No. 16 on year-end lists.

years.src: Wikipedia: Extra Width
years.h: Matador's first Blues Explosion album opens with Afro
years.p: Extra Width was recorded at Doug Easley's studio in Memphis and at Waterworks in New York, and runs 36 minutes.

q: They're the best live band I've ever seen.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: On The Word, Afro reaches British television
years.p: The trio play Afro and History of Sex on Channel 4, the first TV appearance of their career. Presenter Mark Lamarr has a verdict.
years.xp: Afro came out as a UK 7-inch that June, with a video by drummer and filmmaker Tom Surgal.

years.cap: The trio at the Charlotte, Leicester
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Beck takes the trio to Australia and New Zealand
years.p: The Blues Explosion tour both countries with [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]] in August 1994. He'd remix them the following year.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: A stink bomb ends the first live album attempt in Tucson
years.p: Technical trouble had already hit the recording at the DPC in Tucson, Arizona. Then someone in the crowd threw a stink bomb and the band stopped.
years.xp: Some songs from the Tucson session turned up later on the 2010 reissue of Controversial Negro.

years.src: Wikipedia: Orange
years.h: NME and the Village Voice both put Orange at No. 16
years.p: Matador releases Orange on October 11. Bellbottoms opens with a Kurt Hoffman string arrangement, and Pitchfork's Tom Breihan later called the album "an absurd burst of swagger and libido."
years.xp: Bellbottoms came out as a single on February 14, 1995, and went into The Pitchfork 500. AllMusic's Thom Jurek heard "almost entirely new sonic terrain" while the trio's sweaty, hedonistic side stayed up front.

eras.title: Everyone wants in
eras.text: After Orange the band toured with the Beastie Boys, let remixers loose on its songs, drove to a farm in Mississippi to back 69-year-old bluesman R.L. Burnside, and got a video directed by Weird Al Yankovic.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: The Beastie Boys take them to the UK, then across the US with the Roots
years.p: The Blues Explosion play UK shows with the [[Beastie Boys|9beb62b2-88db-4cea-801e-162cd344ee53]] in March 1995, then a US tour with them and [[The Roots|80b3cf5e-18fe-4c59-98c7-e5bb87210710]] in May.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Experimental Remixes lets Beck and Mike D take the songs apart
years.p: Matador's EP hands Blues Explosion songs to [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]], [[Mike D|d3126097-d402-448a-80de-b863c34c735f]], [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]], UNKLE, Dub Narcotic Sound System, and GZA with Killah Priest.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion · Wikipedia: Jon Spencer
years.h: Jon Spencer goes down to Mississippi to play for R.L. Burnside
years.p: At Lunati Farms in Holly Springs, the trio records A Ass Pocket of Whiskey with Burnside and his guitarist Kenny Brown.
years.xp:
Spencer found the day intimidating: "You definitely get the feeling you're playing for him, rather than with him."

Two more songs from the same day, Alice Mae and Highway 7, ended up on Burnside's 1997 album Mr. Wizard. The session sat in the middle of the band's own recording for Now I Got Worry, which moved between Memphis, Los Angeles and Tucson.

years.src: Wikipedia: Orange
years.h: Billboard counts 70,000 copies of Orange
years.p: That's the figure by September 1996, a good number for a Matador band without a bass player.

years.src: Wikipedia: Now I Got Worry
years.h: Rufus Thomas turns up on Now I Got Worry
years.p: Memphis soul veteran [[Rufus Thomas|af1f46fe-903c-4bbf-8e20-a3e114343bd0]] sings on the album, and [[Money Mark|9641c354-53da-4fd5-b8ee-d52e8e1e7e7e]] plays keys on three songs. It reaches No. 50 in the UK.

years.src: Wikipedia: Now I Got Worry
yt: Wail, directed by Weird Al Yankovic
years.h: Weird Al is behind the camera for Wail
years.p: The song is from Now I Got Worry. The director is [[Weird Al Yankovic|7746d775-9550-4360-b8d5-c37bd448ce01]], of all people.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Burnside rides along on the Now I Got Worry tour
years.p: The Blues Explosion take [[R.L. Burnside|355eed00-6c40-4d33-940a-600b2597407a]] through the UK, Europe and the US in October and November 1996.
years.xp: Dutch TV filmed a pre-show jam at the Melkweg in Amsterdam on October 23, and the footage became the video for Boogie Chillun. Six days later they cut a live session at MTV's London studios.

eras.title: Winona Ryder plays Jon Spencer
eras.text: The band's circle widened. A promo-only live record took its name from Public Enemy, Acme passed through a long list of producers, and a music video cast movie stars as the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Controversial Negro, named for a Public Enemy song, goes out promo only
years.p: Vinyl in the US, CD in the UK, and an official Japanese release with five extra tracks.
years.xp: The title comes from Burn Hollywood Burn, from Public Enemy's 1990 album Fear of a Black Planet.

years.src: Wikipedia: Acme
years.h: Acme passes through a lot of hands
years.p: Matador releases it with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], [[Dan the Automator|33945eeb-e2d2-4257-a199-661cbadcf8af]], [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]], Jim Dickinson and Alec Empire among the producers and mixers.
years.xp: Work began with Dan the Automator on a cover of Dr. John's Right Place, Wrong Time for the Scream 2 soundtrack, and the core sessions ran at Albini's Electrical Audio in Chicago in January 1998. A companion EP of B-sides and remixes, Xtra-Acme USA, followed in 1999.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: In the Talk About the Blues video, Winona Ryder plays Jon Spencer
years.p: Directed by Evan Bernard, it casts Winona Ryder, Giovanni Ribisi and John C. Reilly as the band, with the real trio in the picture as detectives.
years.xp: Ryder plays Spencer, Ribisi plays Bauer and Reilly plays Simins. Spencer said he wrote the song right after an interview, "inspired by that and also some of the criticism we've received."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Thieves empty the van at a Vancouver Sheraton
years.p: Gone: microphones, amps, rack gear and Jon Spencer's original 1962 Vanguard theremin, never recovered.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: K Records puts the band in a dancehall with Dub Narcotic
years.p: The full title is Sideways Soul: Dub Narcotic Sound System Meets The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion in a Dancehall Style! It's made with [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]]'s crew.

eras.title: Fewer records, then a long rest
eras.text: The trio worked with outside producers and new labels and shortened its own name for one album. Solomon Burke shared a London stage with them. Then, after playing Orange start to finish, it stopped.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Session drummer Steve Jordan takes the producer's chair
years.p: Plastic Fang is the Blues Explosion's last Matador album. She Said gets a video by Floria Sigismondi.
years.xp: The band played Later... with Jools Holland on the BBC that April. A second She Said video was shot at London's 100 Club on Oxford Street.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Solomon Burke and the trio share the Royal Festival Hall
years.p: A one-off show in London, soul singer [[Solomon Burke|d5c79890-36c5-4f1b-bed3-4468eee093f3]] with the Blues Explosion.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Damage is credited to just the Blues Explosion
years.p: On Sanctuary Records it's the only album under the shortened name. [[Chuck D|88633ac3-c8e2-420f-8415-77ac56b3105f]] guests on Hot Gossip.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Twenty seconds of the band open No Reservations
years.p: They record about a minute of music for Anthony Bourdain's Travel Channel show, and roughly 20 seconds make the opening.

years.src: Wikipedia: Orange
years.h: Orange start to finish at KOKO, then a second set
years.p: At an All Tomorrow's Parties Don't Look Back show in London, the Blues Explosion play the whole album.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: After Damage, the touring stops
years.p: They'd gone through Japan with [[The Kills|2c629b8c-d751-4131-b785-5690bb5e0fd7]] and UK dates supporting [[The Hives|487bfd74-71bf-46dd-b89c-80b7a0f06f2f]]. Then nothing.

eras.title: Back from the dead, with bonus tracks
eras.text: The band came back with a secret show, then a reissue campaign: expanded editions of Extra Width, Orange, Acme, Now I Got Worry, Controversial Negro and Year One. Two more albums followed before one last show in Germany.

years.cap: On stage at Bar Bodega, Wellington, New Zealand
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: A secret show at the Bowery Electric ends the silence
years.p: June 2008, New York. The trio plays the Bowery Electric and the NYC Bicycle Film Festival, then tours Europe that August and September.
years.xp: The European run was billed as the Jukebox Explosion tour.

years.cap: Judah Bauer, Jon Spencer and Russell Simins at Bar Bodega, Wellington, New Zealand
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Shout! Factory reissues the catalog, with extras
years.p: A 22-track retrospective, Dirty Shirt Rock 'n' Roll: The First Ten Years, arrives with the expanded editions. The Now I Got Worry reissue doubles to 32 tracks.
years.xp: Shout! Factory handled the US and Shove! the UK.

years.cap: The Blues Explosion on stage at Bar Bodega, Wellington, New Zealand, January 2011
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Volkswagen wants Black Betty for the Super Bowl
years.p: The band cut the cover at Linear Recording while touring Australia, for a Deutsch L.A. ad that aired on February 6.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Meat + Bone ends an eight-year wait
years.p: The first album since Damage draws praise from Pitchfork, Mojo and The Quietus. That March they'd played Jeff Mangum's All Tomorrow's Parties in Minehead.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Freedom Tower turns out to be the last record
years.p: Freedom Tower: No Wave Dance Party 2015 becomes the Blues Explosion's final studio album.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion
years.h: Nuremberg, March 18, and nobody says it's the last
years.p: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion play their final show in Nuremberg, after extensive touring behind Freedom Tower.

eras.title: Nipped in the bud
eras.text: No one announced a breakup at first. In 2018 Jon Spencer said Judah Bauer's health had put an end to touring, and with it the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Orange
years.h: Bellbottoms opens Baby Driver
years.p: Edgar Wright puts the Orange song in the film's opening sequence and on the official soundtrack.

years.big: "Everything got nipped in the bud when Judah got sick."
years.src: Wikipedia: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion · Wikipedia: Jon Spencer
years.h: Spencer tells the South Bend Tribune the band is over
years.p: Judah Bauer had developed a respiratory problem, Jon Spencer said, and can't go out on a rock and roll tour.
years.xp: Spencer said Bauer was doing better. He went solo that year, then toured as Jon Spencer and the HITmakers with Sam Coomes and [[Janet Weiss|ede4e405-0715-4340-b612-ce79675d4133]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Jon Spencer
years.h: On a podcast, Spencer says the Blues Explosion is no more
years.p: Six years after Nuremberg, Jon Spencer tells the Kreative Kontrol podcast the band is finished, citing Judah Bauer's health.
